name: gputils
why: Assembler, linker and librarian for PIC microcontrollers, a door into old-school embedded toolchains and machine code.

brief.what_it_is: GPUTILS is a collection of command-line tools for Microchip PIC microcontrollers. The homepage names gpasm, gplink and gplib, and the brew executables add gpdasm, gpstrip, gpvc and gpvo. The tools take PIC assembly source and object files and produce linked, relocatable or library output for PIC targets. The homepage does not describe the exact input and output formats of each tool.
brief.why_it_exists: The homepage presents GPUTILS as a free, GPL-licensed toolchain for Microchip PIC microcontrollers. It also says gpsim, a simulator compatible with gputils, exists as a companion project.

commands_seen.context: Checks out the full development source tree over svn+ssh with read/write access, into the current directory (the homepage says it goes into a gputils subdirectory).
Checks out the development source tree read-only over the svn protocol.
Checks out the development source tree over HTTPS with a username.

brief.install_notes: The homepage gives no brew-specific steps. Official source and binary packages come from the SourceForge download page. Compiling from source uses gcc on Linux. Mac OS X builds need the December 2001 Developer Tools, which the page lists as an old requirement. Windows 98/NT builds need MinGW32. The homepage links to many distribution packages (Debian, Fedora, Arch, Gentoo, FreeBSD and others). The MPLAB plugin, gputils-mplab, is Windows-only and needs MPLAB. The homepage does not describe any accounts, runtimes or configuration needed after installation.
brief.standout: It is an old, long-running open-source assembler, linker and librarian for PIC chips, with a Microchip-supplied test suite reformatted and published for regression testing. Its homepage points to a gputils-compatible simulator (gpsim) and several third-party IDEs and GUIs (XGPASM, PiKdev, Piklab).
brief.status: Quiet to maintained, with mixed evidence. The newest news item is 'Jan 30, 2022 -- gputils-1.5.2 Released', which lists experimental gplink features and new PIC16F184XX device support. The page footer says 'Last updated: 2020-01-30', which conflicts with that 2022 news item. The homepage names Molnár Károly as the current primary maintainer. I could not see a commit history or a release page, so I cannot confirm recent activity.
brief.caveats: The homepage does not describe per-tool usage, so I could not confirm flags, options or output formats. The 'Who' section says Borut Ražem supported the project 'until recently' and names only Molnár Károly as current, so maintenance depends on one person. The Mac OS X and Windows 98/NT build notes look dated. The MPLAB plugin works only on Windows. Some features, such as banksel, pagesel and pcallw in gplink, are marked experimental. Microchip's MPASM test files are included in reformatted form, and Microchip provides them without warranty or support. The homepage names the license as 'GNU Public License'; that is the GNU General Public License, and the exact version is not stated. Some links (User Manual, Wiki, FAQ, SourceForge download page) are named in the text but their URLs did not come through in the fetched content.
quotes: GPUTILS is a collection of tools for the Microchip (TM) PIC microcontrollers.
It's distributed under the terms of the GNU Public License.
Linux (and other unixes), Mac OS X, and MS-Windows are supported. GPUTILS will compile natively on Linux using gcc.
fetch_log: https://gputils.sourceforge.io/ — fetched OK. Not a GitHub repo, so this is the only README-equivalent. The page has enough content that I did not follow the linked manuals, wiki or FAQ.
